title: Contextual wear profiles & recall benchmarks (8k/32k/128k)
content:
Summary:
This doc records the experimental design, prompt sets, and aggregated results for the contextual wear / recall benchmarking we ran across three context budgets: 8k, 32k, and 128k. The goal: quantify qualitative degradation modes (recall drop, hallucination up-tick, repetition loops, and attention collapse) when retrieval augmentations and long prefixes interact with model variants and KV-cache strategies. This is an internal onboarding/regression artifact for model candidates being considered for production rollouts.

Motivation / scope:
- Surface regression patterns that are not obvious from token-level loss: e.g., when retrieval chains push older context out of the attention window and the model loses grounding, leading to coherent but incorrect answers.
- Evaluate interaction effects across: model variant (v2.3 baseline vs v3.0 candidate), quantization settings (fp16 vs int8), KV cache retention strategies (full-KV, prefix-bloom, sliding-window), and retrieval chunk size (2k, 8k source docs).
- Focused on retrieval-stress cases (multi-hop references across 10+ docs) and attention-drain tests where repeated entity mentions are intentionally interleaved with distractors.

Datasets & prompt sets (what we used):
1) Synthetic multi-doc narratives (SMD) — 250 cases. Each case stitches 6–12 short docs (~1–3k tokens each) into a coherent timeline. Designed to test long-chain attribution (who did X at time Y).
2) Customer-style KB chains (KB-chain) — 400 cases sampled from anonymized customer KBs (sanitized). Typical case: product spec, changelog, and support ticket thread where the answer requires merging details across remote sections.
3) Code + doc drift set (CODE-DRIFT) — 150 cases where function docstrings appear at the start and updated comments exist near the end of a long file (tests for cross-file reference).
4) Short retrieval anchor probes (ANCHOR) — 200 cases: a short ground-truth sentence inserted near the start; retrieval is configured to return that doc at varying positions to measure hit-rate vs recall.

Prompt design notes:
- All prompts use the same system instruction template used in hosted-api smoke tests (slightly stricter for hallucination penalties).
- We included few-shot examples in half the runs to measure prefix-fidelity under long context. Few-shots were small (2 examples) appended to the very front to intentionally compete for KV capacity.
- Retrieval pipeline: elastic-retriever + reranker. We vary retrieval depth (top-k = 3, 8, 16) and chunking granularity (512-token chunks vs 2k-token chunks).

Methodology / test matrix (high level):
- Model Variants: baseline-v2.3 (prod), candidate-v3.0 (opt kernels)
- Quant: fp16, int8-high, int8-aggressive
- KV strategies: full-KV (retain all), sliding-window (retain last N tokens), prefix-bloom (probabilistic prefix keep)
- Context budgets tested: 8k, 32k, 128k (where 128k runs used streaming and chunked attention to keep latency viable)
- Metrics collected per example: recall@answer-span (exact span overlap), grounding-F1 (token-level), hallucination-rate (binary), repetition-index (ratio of repeated n-grams), latency p50/p95, KV-cache hit/miss ratio, retrieval-hit-rate (was the ground doc returned in top-k?).

Key aggregated results (high-level numbers; see linked artifacts for raw CSVs):
- Recall@answer-span (median across dataset): 8k: 0.82 (v2.3,f16,full-KV), 32k: 0.79, 128k: 0.75.
- Candidate v3.0 shows improved latency (~20% p95) but a small recall regress (median -0.03) on KB-chain for 128k when using int8-aggressive.
- Hallucination-rate increases noticeably at 128k for sliding-window mode: +9 percentage points vs full-KV. Root cause appears tied to older grounding docs being evicted before the final reasoning step.
- Retrieval-hit-rate vs recall: we observed cases where retrieval-hit-rate remained high (>0.9) but recall@answer-span dropped—indicating failure to integrate retrieved evidence rather than retrieval failure.
- KV-cache miss ratio correlation: examples with >0.25 KV miss rate have hallucination-rate 2.3x higher on average.

Notable qualitative failure modes (examples):
- Attention drift: repeated, low-signal distractor paragraphs inserted between anchor facts caused the model to attribute the anchor to the wrong actor. Most prominent at 32k with 2k chunks.
- Smeared evidence: when evidence is interleaved and spans >3 documents, the model sometimes produces a synthesis that mixes facts (e.g., conflating dates). Tends to occur when sliding-window size < 40k tokens (simulated on 128k runs).
- Prefix starvation: few-shot examples appended at the absolute front occasionally suppressed the model's use of mid-context retrieved evidence in 8k runs — likely because early KV entries consumed valuable attention slots.

Regression comparison vs baseline (v2.3 -> v3.0 candidate):
- v3.0 shows consistent latency improvements (p50 down 15–25%, p95 down 10–30%) thanks to new kernel selection.
- Regression signal: on KB-chain at 128k in int8-aggressive, candidate-v3.0 recall -0.06 vs v2.3; hallucination +0.08. Root cause guess: quantization + new kernel ordering interacts poorly with attention sparsity heuristics for very long contexts.
- Mitigation experiment: switching candidate-v3.0 to int8-high reduced the regression to -0.02 recall and hallucination +0.03.

Operator-observable signals (for rollout / monitoring):
- Rising KV-cache miss rate (trend over 1 hour).
- Divergence between retrieval-hit-rate and recall (hit high, recall low) per route.
- Latency/throughput anomalies when switching from 32k->128k contexts (spike in p95 errors).

Recommendations (short-term):
1) For immediate canary, avoid int8-aggressive for v3.0 on KB-heavy routes. Use int8-high or fp16.
2) Implement a lightweight prefix-preservation policy: tag retrieval anchor docs as high-priority so they are kept in KV bloom.
3) Add a regression test to CI with 50 curated KB-chain cases that flag recall drop >0.04 relative to baseline.
4) Improve observability: surface a per-request "integrated-evidence-score" (simple heuristic combining retrieval-hit and KV-hit) to alert when the model is likely to hallucinate.

Longer-term research items / experiments to run:
- Attention reweighting: experiment with dynamic attention prioritization for retrieved documents (boost attention weights for high-relevance spans) and measure impact on recall.
- Chunk-level reranking: rerank retrieval chunks post-tokenization to reduce chunk boundary misses for 2k+ chunk sizes.
- Hybrid retention: combine prefix-bloom with lightweight compression of older KV entries to maintain fidelity without full memory.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO (Evelyn): extract the 50 most representative failure cases and add to the shared regression set (JIRA-1234).
- TODO (Miguel): re-run v3.0 int8-high with sliding-window size = 64k sim on 128k runs and push raw logs to S3 (bucket: s3://redwood-internal/long-context-v3-eval).
- Open: is the hallucination mode in candidate-v3.0 a quantization artifact or an attention scheduling problem? Need a micro-bench that isolates kernel ordering.

Notes for the next sync (applied-ml weekly):
- Bring one flagged failure case to demo (KB-chain #237).
- Propose adding three new monitoring metrics in Console (KV-miss-rate, integrated-evidence-score, retrieval-vs-recall-drift).

References & links:
- Confluence: long-context-evals (see linked artifacts)
- GitHub: runtime PR 987 (kernel reorder)
- Slack thread: #applied-ml-long-context (thread: 2025-01-15 attention-drift)

Appendix (quick example case):
- Example ID: SMD-0042
- Setup: 128k, candidate-v3.0, int8-aggressive, sliding-window(50k), retrieval top-k=8, chunk=2k
- Prompt: 2-shot few-shots at front, then anchor intro paragraph, then 9 source docs interleaved with distractors.
- Expected answer: exact sentence from doc 3.
- Model output: plausible multi-sentence summary that cites info from doc 7 (wrong) and invents a date.
- Observed signals: retrieval-hit-rate=0.95 (doc 3 in top-8), KV-miss ratio=0.32, p95 latency 1.6s (acceptable).
- Conclusion: evidence existed but was not integrated; likely eviction or attended-weight failure.

If you're reviewing: please add comments inline for any missing experiment variants you think are important. I'll prioritize creating the 50-case repro set once we align on which mitigation (quant vs retention policy) to try first.
